Q1: Which callers should the fix cover?
Choices:
A) Only the SUMMARISER call in `scripts/summarize_reviewer_consensus.sh`, as the finding cites.
B) Fix it in the engine (`claude_run` / the read-profile settings in `scripts/claude_engine.py`). That covers every read-profile Claude role: SUMMARISER, BEHAVIOURAL_SMOKE, the read-mode RB_JUDGE, CLARIFY, PLAN and the other read-only roles, since they share the same unrestricted `Read`/`Grep`/`Glob`. (RECOMMENDED)
C) Option B, plus the write-profile roles (`bypassPermissions`), which can read the same files.
**Note:** Option A leaves the same weakness in every other read-profile role, so the weekly audit would likely file it again for those callers.
Q2: How should credential files be kept out of the model's reach?
Choices:
A) Permission deny rules only. Add `Read`/`Grep`/`Glob` (and Bash) deny entries to the rendered Claude settings for the token-pool directory, `**/.git/config`, `/proc/*/environ` and the runner's home and temp credential paths. Small change, but it relies on the CLI enforcing those rules.
B) Filesystem isolation, as the finding recommends. Run the read-profile Claude call against a credential-free snapshot of the source (no `.git/config` with an auth header, no `extraheader`), and keep the token-pool directory outside anything the model can reach. Pass the OAuth token to the CLI only through the process environment, and also block `/proc` environment reads.
C) Both: isolation (B) as the main control, plus deny rules (A) as an extra layer. (RECOMMENDED)
